brow: Aggregated snapshot · open-source compilation · not official reporting
editionNote: Evening edition. It covers the 24 hours to 17:10 CEST on 20 October; new research covers 05:10 CEST to 17:10 CEST on 20 October, items from the previous edition still inside the 24 hours were carried, and stories with new developments are marked as follow-ups.

theaters.heading: Battlefield, long-range strikes, and peace diplomacy in Russia's war on Ukraine

items.title: Zelensky Meets Witkoff in Oslo, with Kushner Joining by Video
items.lede: Zelensky held talks in Oslo on 20 October with US envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, and Axios reported the aim was a peace proposal for Russia.

sections.text: Zelensky arrived in Oslo on 20 October for talks with US special envoy Steve Witkoff, with Jared Kushner joining by videoconference, the Norwegian government said, as reported by NBC News [1][2]. Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre and Finnish President Alexander Stubb were also due to take part, and Støre said Zelensky had asked Oslo and Helsinki to organise the meeting 'at a critical time for Ukraine' [3][1]. Axios reported that officials from the UK, France, Germany, and Poland, plus EU and NATO staff, would attend, and that the aim was to draft a peace proposal to present to Russia; an unnamed US official said Witkoff plans to visit Russia afterwards to meet Putin [4]. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said he hoped Trump's envoys could meet in Russia 'in the near future' but gave no date [1]. Zelensky also met King Haakon VIII and discussed the return of children taken by Russia and the situation in occupied Oleshky [5]. No readout of the talks' outcome was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is high that the Oslo meeting took place with these participants, because the Norwegian government, NBC News, the BBC, and Ukrainian outlets agree. Confidence on Witkoff's planned Moscow trip is moderate, because it rests on one anonymous US official quoted by Axios.

items.title: Russian Drones Kill Seven around Kyiv; Outages Hit 12 Regions
items.lede: Air defences downed or jammed 115 of 165 drones, but hits at 30 locations brought hourly power cuts nationwide, Ukraine's Air Force and Ukrenergo said.

sections.text: Russia launched 165 drones, 105 of them jet-powered, plus missiles and decoys at Ukraine from 18:00 Kyiv time (17:00 CEST) on 19 October, and air defences downed or jammed 115 by morning, Ukraine's Air Force said [6]. It recorded hits at 30 locations [6]. Ukrenergo said new outages followed in 12 regions, including Lviv, Odesa, Kharkiv, and Zaporizhzhia, with hourly power cuts nationwide through the day [7]. In Kyiv Oblast's Obukhiv district, a man and two women were killed and six people injured at a production and storage building, Governor Tymur Tkachenko said [8]. A drone strike near the Kyiv-Odesa road in Chabany, by a shopping centre, killed three and injured four, prosecutors said [9]. In Kyiv city, a drone that crashed near a petrol station in Holosiivskyi district killed one person and injured seven, Mayor Vitali Klitschko and the city health department said [10][11]. No Russian Defence Ministry comment was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is high on the scale of the attack and the outages, because the Air Force and Ukrenergo state them on record. Confidence on the Kyiv-area tolls is high for the city crash, which two outlets and two officials report, and moderate for Obukhiv and Chabany, which rest on one outlet each.

items.title: Russian Shelling of Kramatorsk Kills Three Heat Plant Workers
items.lede: Russian shelling of Kramatorsk on 20 October killed three men and injured two people, the Donetsk Oblast prosecutor's office said.

sections.text: Russian forces shelled Kramatorsk in Donetsk Oblast at 10:04 Kyiv time (09:04 CEST) on 20 October, killing three men aged 42, 47, and 48 and injuring a woman and a 38-year-old man, the Donetsk Oblast prosecutor's office said [12][13]. Prosecutors said the weapon type was being established and opened a war-crimes case [12]. Three apartment blocks were damaged [13]. Roman Polishchuk, head of the municipal utility Kramatorskteploenerho, told the portal EnerhoReforma that the three dead were employees of the city's combined heat and power plant, killed while on duty [13]. No Russian comment was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is high on the strike and the toll, because the prosecutor's statement is on record and two outlets report it. Confidence that all three dead were plant workers is moderate, because it rests on the utility head's account in one outlet.

items.title: Vance Says Ukraine Should Not Join NATO or Strike Russian Refineries
items.lede: Vance argued that strikes on Russian diesel production raise energy prices for Americans, speaking after Trump accused Zelensky of not wanting to end the war.

sections.text: US Vice President JD Vance said in an interview with 2WAY TONIGHT that Ukraine is a partner 'in a certain sense' but that US and Ukrainian interests diverge at times [14]. He said Ukraine should not be striking Russian diesel production, because it raises energy prices for Americans [14][15]. 'They're not in NATO. I don't think that they should be in NATO,' Vance said [15]. The remarks came after Trump accused Zelensky of not wanting to end the war [14]. No Ukrainian government response to the interview was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high that Vance made these remarks, because two outlets quote the same interview consistently.

items.title: Rubio Says Patriot Delays Not Political as WP Reports Hegseth Holdup
items.lede: Zelensky says Washington has approved only some of the Patriot interceptors Ukraine bought through NATO's PURL scheme, and no Pentagon statement was found.

sections.text: Zelensky said on 18 and 19 October that Washington had approved only some of the Patriot interceptors bought for Ukraine through NATO's PURL scheme and pointed at the Pentagon [16][17]. On 20 October the Washington Post, citing a US official and three others, reported that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has not formally rejected the allied Patriot transfers but has not taken the steps to approve them, as summarised by Ukrinform [18]. Zelensky said he held a 'constructive' call with Secretary of State Marco Rubio on interceptors, early warning, and Starlink and Starshield services [19]. Speaking in India, Rubio said deliveries may have been delayed but there was no 'deliberate political directive' to harm Ukraine [20]. He called claims that Ukrainians are dying because the US withholds warnings 'scandalous' and said gaps on 13 and 18 October were a technical matter under review [21][3]. On 19 October Zelensky also met a Lockheed Martin team on interceptor supply [22]. No Pentagon statement was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is high that Zelensky and Rubio made these statements, because they are on record and several outlets carry them. Confidence that Hegseth is holding up approval is moderate, because it now rests on anonymous US and Ukrainian sources in two outlets, and no Pentagon statement was found.

items.title: Man Opens Fire in Kyiv Draft Office, Wounding Three Police and Three Soldiers
items.lede: A man brought to a Kyiv recruitment centre for violating mobilisation law opened fire inside on 19 October, wounding six people before police detained him.

sections.text: A man brought to a Territorial Recruitment Centre in Kyiv's Pechersk district for violating mobilisation law opened fire inside the building at about 19:00 local time (18:00 CEST) on 19 October, Kyiv police said [23][24]. Three police officers and three service members were wounded and taken to hospital, and the shooter was detained [23]. Police said an investigation is under way and the circumstances are being established [23]. The Kyiv Independent noted earlier attacks on recruiters this year, including a fatal stabbing in Lviv and a shooting in Odesa in August [24]. No details on the shooter's identity or weapon had been released by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the shooting, the six wounded, and the detention, because the police statement and two outlets agree.

items.title: Pope Leo XIV Calls Zelensky on Oleshky, Days after Speaking with Putin
items.lede: Pope Leo XIV discussed occupied Oleshky and a humanitarian ceasefire with Zelensky by phone on 19 October, the Holy See said, as reported by Ukrainska Pravda.

sections.text: Pope Leo XIV spoke by phone with Zelensky on 19 October, three days after his call with Vladimir Putin, the Holy See Press Office said, as reported by Ukrainska Pravda [25]. The pope discussed the situation in Russian-occupied Oleshky in Kherson Oblast and referred to the 'humanitarian ceasefire' he had raised with Putin [25]. The Holy See said he hoped cooperation between both sides would allow food and medical aid deliveries and the voluntary, safe evacuation of civilians [25]. Zelensky said he briefed the pope on Russia's escalating attacks and that Kyiv is 'preparing decisions' on helping people in Oleshky [25]. No Kremlin comment on the call was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate, because one outlet carrying the Holy See and Zelensky statements was read; the Holy See post itself was not opened.

items.title: Russian Drone Kills at Least Five, Including Children, in Kharkiv Oblast Park
items.lede: Regional police report 15 injured, including seven children, in the 19 October strike on Nova Vodolaha and have opened a war-crimes case.

sections.text: A Russian drone hit the central park in Nova Vodolaha, Kharkiv Oblast, at about 16:30 local time (15:30 CEST) on 19 October, while families with children were there, the regional prosecutor's office and Interior Minister Ivan Vyhivskyi said [26][27]. Prosecutors said a Geran-3 drone was used [26]. Governor Oleh Syniehubov first put the dead at six, including three children, then revised it to five: three women aged 28, 34, and 36, and two girls, whom Interfax-Ukraine reported as aged 11 and about one [28]. The regional police also list five dead, three women and two girls, and 15 injured, including seven children, and opened a war-crimes case [29]. A later Kyiv Independent update citing Syniehubov gives six dead, including a man of about 40, and gives the older girl's age as eight [27]. Zelensky called it an 'absolute atrocity' and asked partners not to lift sanctions on Russia [27]. No Russian Defence Ministry comment was found by the cutoff.

Confidence that the strike happened and killed civilians, including children, is high, because police, prosecutors, and several outlets report it. Confidence on the death toll is moderate, because official figures moved between five and six and sources still differ, including on the older girl's age.

items.title: Russian Strike on Khmelnytskyi Kills Two Women and Injures Three
items.lede: Homes were damaged, a business caught fire, and some consumers lost power after a line was hit, regional governor Serhii Tiurin said.

sections.text: Two women were killed and three people injured in a Russian attack on Khmelnytskyi on 19 October, regional governor Serhii Tiurin said, as reported by Ukrainska Pravda [30]. Residential buildings were damaged, a business caught fire, and some consumers lost power after a line was hit [30]. Search and rescue work ended at 20:28 local time (19:28 CEST) [30]. No weapon type had been given by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate, because one outlet carrying the governor's statement was read.

items.title: WSJ: Republicans Threaten Pentagon Funding over Trump's Russia Policy
items.lede: Several pro-Ukraine Republicans are threatening to withhold support for Pentagon funding unless Trump takes a tougher line on Russia, Ukrinform reported, citing the Wall Street Journal.

sections.text: Several pro-Ukraine Republicans are threatening to withhold support for Pentagon funding unless President Trump takes a tougher line on Russia, Ukrinform reported, citing the Wall Street Journal [31]. Congressman Don Bacon warned that Congress would not back Trump's legislative agenda without action against Russia, and wrote on X that reducing intelligence sharing and Starlink access for Ukraine 'equates to aiding the invader' [31]. Congressman Brian Fitzpatrick told the paper the administration would face 'consequences' unless Ukraine's satellite access is restored [31]. The dispute comes as the Pentagon seeks a $350 billion supplemental package and a $1.5 trillion defence budget [31]. No White House response was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate, because the report rests on one agency's summary of the Wall Street Journal article, which was not read directly.

theaters.heading: Sabotage, drones, cyber, disinformation, and espionage targeting European states

items.title: Poland Detains Polish-Ukrainian Reservist on Suspicion of Spying
items.lede: Deputy Defence Minister Cezary Tomczyk said the man had been conducting reconnaissance of military installations, and he faces up to eight years in prison, Notes from Poland reported.

sections.text: Poland's military police confirmed on 19 October that they had detained a 31-year-old reservist with Polish and Ukrainian citizenship, a senior private in the reserve, on suspicion of offering to work for a foreign intelligence service against Poland, Notes from Poland reported [1]. Military police in Łódź detained him on 16 October while he was on a course at the Military Medical Academy, and he has been placed in custody for three months [1]. The offence carries up to eight years in prison [1]. Deputy Defence Minister Cezary Tomczyk said the man had been conducting reconnaissance of certain Polish military installations [1]. The authorities have not named the foreign service involved.
Confidence is moderate, because one outlet carrying military police and ministerial statements was read; the military police post itself was not opened.

items.title: NATO Council Sets Black Sea Talks after Romania Downs Two Drones
items.lede: NATO's North Atlantic Council was set to discuss Black Sea security on 20 October at Romania's request, after Romania shot down two Geran drones.

sections.text: Romania asked for a North Atlantic Council meeting on Black Sea security after two drones were shot down over its territorial waters on 17 October, at 18:01 and 18:05, the first two minutes after entering Romanian airspace [2][3]. The defence ministry identified them as Geran attack drones and said Romania has shot down six this year [2]. A NATO official told Euronews România that the council would discuss the issue on the afternoon of 20 October during its weekly session [4]. President Nicușor Dan said the situation resembles last year's drone incursions along the Danube, that new equipment is needed, and that Russia is trying to destabilise Romania, Bulgaria, and other eastern-flank states and weaken support for Ukraine [4]. Moldovan police said a drone fell in a northern district; its origin was not stated [5]. No NATO statement on the meeting's outcome was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is high that the council scheduled the discussion for 20 October and on the shoot-downs, because a NATO official and Romanian ministers state them on record and several outlets agree. Confidence on the Moldovan drone is low, because only one outlet reports it.

items.title: Bulgaria Issues European Warrants for Two Germans over Starlink Antenna Arson
items.lede: A Sofia court authorised European arrest warrants for two German nationals charged in absentia with setting fire to Starlink antennas at a teleport near Sofia.

sections.text: The Sofia City Court on Monday authorised European arrest warrants for two German nationals, named by prosecutors as Zeka Islam and Tirpan Beytullah, who were charged in absentia on 14 October with setting fire to Starlink antennas at the Plana teleport south of Sofia, the state news agency BTA reported [6]. Prosecutors said the two, holding German documents showing they were born in 2007, entered on 9 October, set the fire at about 22:25 local time, and left for Serbia in a German-registered car [6]. BTA said three antennas were destroyed, two partly damaged, and three otherwise affected; BNT said 18 antennas were set on fire [6][7]. German authorities do not know where the two are [6][7]. Defence lawyers said the car, not the men, had been identified and that they would appeal [6]. No official attribution of the attack to a state was found by the cutoff. DW, citing AFP and dpa, said both suspects are 19 and noted that a similar Polish Starlink case led to four arrests in Germany [8].

Confidence that the court authorised the warrants is high, because the state news agency, the public broadcaster, and DW report it. Confidence on how many antennas were hit is moderate, because BTA and BNT give different figures.

items.title: Assessment Says Russia and Iran Exploit French Riots with Fake Reports
items.lede: The assessment found no evidence that a foreign state started or directs the unrest, calling it 'a home-grown protest movement', National Security News reported.

sections.text: A 15-page assessment by the Disinformation Commission, dated 18 October, says Russian-linked networks and Iranian officials have spread misleading claims and fabricated news reports to portray France as descending into chaos, National Security News reported [9]. The assessment found no evidence that a foreign state started or directs the unrest, calling it 'a home-grown protest movement' [9]. It said the widest distortion came from far-right influencers in France and abroad who passed off old videos as the riots [9]. It also warned that Russian propaganda appeared among sources retrieved by AI search engines [9]. No response from Moscow or Tehran was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is low, because one outlet reports the assessment, the document itself was not read, and the commission's makeup is not described in the report.

theaters.heading: Politics, security, and defense across the EU and NATO's European members

items.title: Portuguese Police Clear Housing-Protest Camps in Lisbon and Porto, Detaining 55
items.lede: All 55 detainees were freed by early afternoon, and the Acampada movement vowed to return as new protests were called in both cities, Observador reported.

sections.text: Portugal's PSP police cleared housing-protest tent camps in Lisbon's Rossio square and in Porto early on Tuesday, giving protesters a few minutes to leave, Observador reported [1]. The PSP said it detained 55 people in Lisbon, where it said protesters resisted orders, made no arrests in Porto, and reported two people lightly hurt [1]. Police called their action 'calm, proportional, and adequate, without use of the baton', although Observador said images showed batons in use [1]. All 55 were released by early afternoon [1]. Interior Minister Luís Neves said 'the camps are over', warned that extremist conduct would be repressed, and urged protesters not to let extremists infiltrate them [1]. The Acampada movement said it would return, and new protests were called for 19:00 Lisbon time in Lisbon and Porto [1].

Confidence on the clearances and the 55 detentions is moderate, because police and the minister gave them on record but they were read in one outlet. Confidence on baton use is low, because police deny it and only one outlet describes images.

items.title: Nuñez Orders Prefects to Ban Risky Saturday Protests as Policing Draws Fire
items.lede: Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez told prefects to ban protests likely to disturb order on 24 October and consider targeted curfews, according to a telegram BFMTV saw.

sections.text: The BBC saw riot police baton a crowd in central Paris on Saturday, and BBC Verify counted at least 11 baton blows on five apparently unarmed protesters [2][3]. In Saint-Étienne a 17-year-old lost a hand to a grenade, and in Mulhouse a 17-year-old girl lost an eye; police inspectorates are investigating [4][5][6]. In parliament on Tuesday, Lecornu blamed an 'insurrectional scheme' by far-left groups, said intelligence 'did not see everything', and said the Paris deployment was too static [7]. He and Nuñez promised a 'massive' deployment for Saturday, and Nuñez said Sentinelle soldiers would take over static guard duties to free police [7]. In a telegram seen by BFMTV, Nuñez told prefects to ban protests likely to disturb order on Saturday 24 October, route others away from public buildings and shopping streets, and consider targeted curfews [7]. Yellow Vest representatives have called protests for that day [8]. No new baton charges on 19 or 20 October were found by the cutoff.

Confidence on the weekend baton use is high, because BBC reporters saw it and BBC Verify checked footage. Confidence on the parliamentary statements is high, because they were made in public. Confidence on the telegram is moderate, because only BFMTV reports seeing it.

items.title: France Renews Targeted Curfews after Calm First Night
items.lede: Lyon, Bordeaux, Nice, and other French towns kept or renewed partial curfews after police said the first night under them passed without major incidents.

sections.text: Partial curfews took effect on Monday night after Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu let local authorities impose them; he ruled out whole-city curfews [9][10][11]. Paris police barred anyone from Place de la République and Les Halles from 23:00 to 06:00, and Lyon, Nice, Bordeaux, Lille, and other towns set partial or youth curfews [12][10][13][14]. Police said the night passed without major incidents, and Lecornu wrote on X on Tuesday that the curfews 'contributed to calm' and that prefects and mayors would decide new ones for Tuesday night [15][8]. Bordeaux and Nice kept their curfews for several days, and the Rhône prefecture renewed Lyon's city-centre curfew from 21:00 to 06:00 [15][7]. Paris police banned carrying fuel in individual containers, protective gear near schools, and fireworks until Thursday [7]. The Créteil Soleil shopping centre closed on Tuesday afternoon after looting rumours on social media caused a crowd surge, the Paris police prefecture said [7]. Macron refused Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez's resignation [16][17]. In parliament, Nuñez denied Mediapart's report that intelligence officers were pressed to blame LFI [7][13].

Confidence on the curfew orders and the calm night is high, because officials announced them and Euronews, RFI, and BFMTV agree. Confidence on the Créteil closure and the Paris bans is moderate, because they were read in BFMTV only.

items.title: Storm Adam Death Toll in Spain Rises to Seven as Sánchez Visits Oliva
items.lede: Firefighters recovered a man's body off Menorca, Antena 3 reported, and Sánchez faced shouts of 'resign' on his visit to the flood-hit town.

sections.text: Storm Adam's toll rose to seven on Tuesday after firefighters in Menorca recovered the body of a man aged 60 to 70 from the sea, Antena 3 reported [18]. Earlier counts gave four dead: two in Oliva, a man who drowned at Sagunto beach, and a woman swept into a stream in Catalonia [19][20]; a rockfall killed a driver in Benaoján, Málaga [21]. Valencia's regional government confined more than 850,000 people in 145 municipalities on Monday, La Vanguardia reported [21]; Al Jazeera put the figure at 800,000 on Monday morning, cut to 87,000 in eight municipalities by late afternoon [19]. Security forces made more than 400 rescues in the region [19]. Up to 700 litres of rain per square metre fell in places [19]. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez visited Oliva on Tuesday amid shouts of 'resign' and said the storms were reaching an intensity Spain had not known [18].
Confidence on the first four deaths is high, because officials gave them and several outlets agree. Confidence on the total of seven is low to moderate, because it was read in one live page.

items.title: France Jails 149 Rioters as Custody Count Passes 2,500
items.lede: Justice Minister Gérald Darmanin has told prosecutors to treat riot cases as organized crime, allowing 72-hour custody, and says more than 800 people have been referred to court.

sections.text: Justice Minister Gérald Darmanin said at Lille's court at about 12:39 on Tuesday that 149 suspected rioters or looters had been jailed, on remand or by immediate sentence [7]. Le Parisien, with AFP, quoted him as saying about 150 were jailed and more than 800 referred to court [22]. Earlier on Tuesday the Justice Ministry put the jailed at 123 and custody at more than 2,500 since Saturday [8][23]. On Monday night Darmanin had given 2,513 in custody and 67 jailed, and told prosecutors to treat cases as organized crime, allowing 72-hour custody [13]. A 40-year-old man with ultra-left ties was arrested on Tuesday over the arson of Limoges city hall, and an anti-terrorism unit leads that inquiry, AFP reported, citing a source [8]. The BBC said officials put injured police at about 1,000 [11]. Medef head Patrick Martin said the state 'failed' and at least 3,000 businesses were hit, by preliminary estimates [8][15]. About 550,000 people marched on Saturday by official count; organisers claimed 800,000 [24].

Confidence on the custody and jail figures is high, because the justice minister and his ministry gave them on record. Confidence on the Limoges arrest is moderate, because it rests on one AFP source. Confidence on business losses is moderate, because they are preliminary estimates.

items.title: Italy Sends 500 Troops to Milan as Cabinet Readies Riot Decree
items.lede: Italy is sending 500 extra soldiers to Milan after weekend riots, and its cabinet was due to take up a public-order decree on Tuesday.

sections.text: Italy's government is sending 500 extra soldiers to Milan and vowed a 'firm response from the state' after weekend riots, The Guardian reported on Tuesday [25]. Milan police detained 271 young people after looting near the Duomo on Saturday and Sunday; 32 were arrested, including 23 minors, and 28 were arrested in Turin [25]. ANSA reported on Monday evening that the cabinet would take up a public-order decree on Tuesday [26], and Il Tempo said the meeting was set for 17:30 [27]. Il Tempo, citing draft text, said it creates an aggravated group-damage offence carrying 18 months to five years, allows arrests within 48 hours based on video, lets police hold people judged dangerous for up to 12 hours, and fines parents of offenders under 14 [27]. No curfew appeared in the reported draft; Monday reports had said Meloni was weighing one [10]. A new '17 October' movement called protests every Saturday in Milan and other cities [25]. No adopted decree text was found by the cutoff.

Confidence on the troop deployment and detention figures is high, because police and ministers gave them and The Guardian and Italian outlets agree. Confidence on the decree's contents is moderate, because they come from a leaked draft before cabinet approval.

theaters.heading: Security, politics, and Russian pressure on Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania

items.title: NATO Tests Counter-Drone and Deep-Strike Technology at Latvian Ranges
items.lede: Nearly 100 defence companies from more than 20 countries take part, and the series ends with a NATO FUSE event in late October, Latvia's Defence Ministry said.

sections.text: A series of NATO experiments and trials of new defence technologies began in Latvia this week at the Ādaži base and the Sēlija military ranges, Latvia's Defence Ministry said, LSM reported on 20 October [1]. The work covers the Digital Backbone Experiment (DiBaX 2026) on communications, counter-drone sensor and effector tests under the Layered Counter UAS Initiative, and Next Generation Targeting tests for deep strike [1]. Nearly 100 defence companies from more than 20 countries and allied forces take part, and the series is led by NATO's Allied Command Transformation with Latvia's Defence Ministry, armed forces, and LMT Defence [1]. Defence Minister Raivis Melnis said the fifth DiBaX shows Latvia can host such testing, and the series ends with a NATO FUSE event at the end of October [1].
Confidence is moderate, because one public broadcaster relays the Defence Ministry's release; the release itself was not read.

items.title: airBaltic Prepares Mass Redundancies as Collective Deal Fails
items.lede: airBaltic's chairman said on 20 October the airline expects mass redundancies soon, after staff and management failed to agree on collectively reduced hours.

sections.text: Latvia's national airline airBaltic expects mass redundancies in the near future, board chairman Andrejs Martinovs told Latvian Radio on 20 October, LSM reported [2]. He declined to give a number, saying some staff were leaving voluntarily; the airline has previously spoken of 500 to 700 job losses [2]. Martinovs said a collective agreement to move staff to part-time or 85 percent hours could not be reached, so employees may now apply individually for reduced hours [2]. The fleet will shrink to 36 aircraft by year-end before growing to 40 by 2030, and the airline has begun Chapter 11 restructuring in the United States, LSM said [2]. No final redundancy figure was published by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate, because one public broadcaster reports the chairman's on-record interview and the job-loss range comes from the airline's earlier statements; no company release was read.

items.title: Lithuania Seeks NATO Rule Change to Shoot Down Unseen Drones
items.lede: Lithuania's prime minister asked NATO to let fighter jets shoot down airspace violators pilots cannot see, after a diverted Ukrainian drone crashed in Lithuania.

sections.text: Defence Minister Robertas Kaunas said on 18 October that the drone that crashed in the Pasvalys district was a Ukrainian FPV-1 drone diverted into Lithuania by Russian electronic warfare, and that Ukraine had apologised [3]. Poland's Defence Ministry denied a Polish media report that the drone was launched inside Lithuania and said it was reviewing radar data with Lithuania [4]. Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevičius told LRT he had asked for consultations with NATO on changing procedures so that fighter jets can shoot down objects violating Lithuanian airspace even when pilots cannot see them, LRT reported on 20 October [5]. He said NATO jets were scrambled on Sunday but the pilots did not see the object and so did not fire, and that a revised procedure would 'probably be implemented within a month' [5]. Under current rules pilots may not use force without visual identification, LRT said [5]. No NATO response to the request was found by the cutoff.

Confidence that the drone was Ukrainian is high, because Lithuanian and Polish defence officials say so on the record. Confidence on the request to NATO is high on the fact of the request, because the prime minister made it on the record to the public broadcaster; no NATO statement was read.

items.title: Estonia's Parliament Rejects No-Confidence Motion Against Michal Government
items.lede: The motion won 34 votes when at least 51 were needed, with the Social Democrats not voting, according to the parliament and ERR.

sections.text: A motion of no confidence in Prime Minister Kristen Michal's government failed in the Riigikogu on 19 October, with 34 MPs voting for it when at least 51 votes were needed, the parliament said [6]. No MPs voted against or abstained; the Social Democrats and some unaffiliated MPs, among them Tõnis Mölder, did not join the motion and did not vote, ERR reported [7]. The motion was signed by 34 opposition MPs [7]. Isamaa leader Urmas Reinsalu, speaking for the initiators, said the government had lost credibility, its sense of reality, and broad public support, and that Social Democratic support would keep Michal in office [6]. Michal rejected the criticism, citing economic growth twice the EU average, rising deposits, and lower unemployment and inflation, and called the motion an irresponsible political manoeuvre [8].
Confidence is high, because the vote count comes from the parliament's own release and is matched by the public broadcaster.

theaters.heading: Stability, politics, and outside influence in the Western Balkans

items.title: Montenegro Adopts Constitutional Integrity Checks for Prime Minister and Ministers
items.lede: The ruling coalition, independent MPs, and one opposition MP backed the change, and the government agreed a law will set out how checks are done, Balkan Insight reported.

sections.text: Montenegro's parliament late on 19 October adopted constitutional amendments requiring integrity checks on candidates for prime minister and cabinet posts before nomination, to identify conflicts of interest, Balkan Insight reported [1]. The ruling coalition, independent MPs, and one opposition European Alliance MP backed it; the Democratic Party of Socialists and the Democratic People's Party were absent [1]. The government also accepted a demand for a further amendment requiring a law to set out how checks are done [1]. Deputy Prime Minister Momo Koprivica said 'anyone who wants to run the state cannot do business with the state' [1]. No final vote count was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate, because one regional outlet reports the vote; no parliament release was read.

items.title: Serbian Filmmakers to File Criminal Complaint Against Culture Minister Selaković
items.lede: The associations put the initial damage at €17 million, with dozens of films not made, and allege funding was withheld to punish critics of corruption, N1 reported.

sections.text: Seven Serbian filmmaker associations said they would file a criminal complaint with the Public Prosecutor's Office for Organised Crime against Culture Minister Nikola Selaković and alleged accomplices for undermining the national film industry, N1 reported [2]. Miloš Škundrić, president of the Association of Film Directors of Serbia, told Danas the initial damage was €17 million, with dozens of films not made because state funding had been withheld for more than two years [2]. The associations allege the funding was withheld in retaliation against filmmakers who criticised corruption [2]. No Culture Ministry response was found by the cutoff, and the complaint had not been confirmed as filed.
Confidence is moderate, because one outlet relays the associations' statement and a Danas interview; neither was read directly.

items.title: Kosovo Risks Losing €90 Million More in EU Growth Plan Funds
items.lede: The money is lost unless 23 reforms are finished by the end of December, Balkan Insight reported.

sections.text: Kosovo forfeited €40 million in EU Growth Plan funding in June and risks losing about €90 million more unless 23 reforms are done by the end of December, Balkan Insight reported on 20 October [3]. Kosovo's head of negotiations with the EU, Jeton Zulfaj, said all required reforms must be implemented by then [3]. Of its €882.6 million allocation, Pristina has received only €61.8 million in pre-financing, about 7 percent, after nearly two years of deadlock and three elections in two years delayed ratification [3]. No European Commission statement on the deadline was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate, because one regional outlet reports the figures and Zulfaj's statement; no Commission or Kosovo government document was read.

items.title: N1 Bars Vučić from Presenting His Election List; Ruling Party Calls It Fascist
items.lede: N1 Television refused to let Aleksandar Vučić present his list in its election slot, and Vučić and Ana Brnabić called the decision fascist.

sections.text: N1 Television refused to let Aleksandar Vučić represent the 'Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia' list in its slot for presenting electoral lists on Wednesday, saying he had refused to appear on N1 for years while calling its staff 'scum, terrorists, and foreign mercenaries' [4]. The newsroom invited the Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) to send another representative and said it would interview Vučić only after the 25 October elections [4]. Vučić and Ana Brnabić called the decision fascist, and SNS had not said whether anyone else would present the list, Vreme reported [5]. No SNS nominee for the slot was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high, because N1's own statement and Vreme's report agree on the refusal and the reaction.

items.title: Albania's Protests Reach Eighth Day as Police Report 271 Arrests
items.lede: Student-led protests against Prime Minister Edi Rama entered an eighth day on 20 October, and Tirana police said 271 people had been arrested in seven days.

sections.text: Student-led protests demanding Prime Minister Edi Rama's resignation entered an eighth day in Tirana on 20 October [6]. On 19 October protesters clashed with police, who used water and tear gas [7]. Tirana police said on 20 October they had arrested 33 people and prosecuted 41 others over that rally, that seven officers were hurt, and that 271 people had been arrested over seven days [8]. The Supreme Court postponed all non-urgent hearings after the 17 October fire damaged its premises and court files [9]. Rama said some students were bound to 'politically extremist ideologies', Balkan Insight reported [10]. The Teachers' Union announced a boycott of teaching at all universities from 21 October [11]. The OSCE's ODIHR urged police to avoid unlawful or disproportionate force [6]. President Bajram Begaj met the US, EU, and German ambassadors [12]. DW put injuries since the protests began at about 300, more than half of them police [13].

Confidence on the arrest counts is moderate, because they come from a police statement relayed by CNA; the police release itself was not read. Confidence on the court closure, union boycott, and ODIHR's call is moderate, because CNA alone relays them. Confidence on Rama's remarks is high, because Balkan Insight reports them from a public meeting.

items.title: KRIK Says 15 Serbian Narcotics Officers Sidelined after Record Marijuana Seizure
items.lede: Fifteen Serbian narcotics officers were moved out of their division after seizing five tons of marijuana on a ruling-party councillor's farm, KRIK reported, according to N1.

sections.text: Fifteen ranking officers of the narcotics division of Serbia's Criminal Police Directorate (UKP) were moved out of the division after they seized five tons of marijuana in Konjuh near Kruševac, on a farm owned by a local councillor of the ruling Serbian Progressive Party (SNS), the investigative outlet KRIK reported, N1 said [14]. KRIK obtained a letter the officers sent to Prime Minister Đuro Macut saying UKP chief Marko Kričak had 'destroyed' the division and that they faced retaliation [14]. Former division head Radomir Popović was reassigned to the War Crimes Division and his deputy Nikola Đoković to the Traffic Police [14]. The team also helped North Macedonia seize a further 40 tons of narcotics linked to the same group, and police estimated losses to it at more than €150 million [14]. No Interior Ministry or police response was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate, because one outlet relays KRIK's investigation and the officers' letter; the letter itself was not read and no official response was found.

items.title: Kobakhidze Says EU Backs Georgian Protesters but Urges Calm in France
items.lede: Kobakhidze, who also cited Albania, called Europe's description of violent Georgian protesters as peaceful a 'farce', OC Media reported.

sections.text: Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze accused European officials of a double standard, saying they urged protesters in France and Albania to refrain from violence while encouraging demonstrators in Georgia, OC Media reported on 20 October [1]. 'There is clearly a double standard here. Not only regarding France, but even Albania,' he told journalists, calling Europe's description of violent Georgian protesters as peaceful a 'farce' [1]. Tbilisi Mayor and Georgian Dream leader Kakha Kaladze also accused European officials of encouraging violent groups in Georgia [1]. No EU response was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate, because one outlet reports the remarks; no video or transcript was read.

items.title: Aliyev Signs Order Establishing Karabakh National Park
items.lede: Azerbaijan's President Ilham Aliyev ordered the creation of a Karabakh National Park, APA reported, without giving its boundaries, area, or management body.

sections.text: Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev signed an order establishing Karabakh National Park, APA reported on 20 October [2]. The report gave no boundaries, area, or management body [2]. No Armenian government reaction was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate, because one Azerbaijani agency reports the order and the order text was not read.

items.title: Gakharia's For Georgia Asks Court to Split Its Case from Party-Ban Suit
items.lede: Executive secretary Berdia Sichinava called the bid to ban the only opposition party in parliament 'absurd and devoid of any legal basis', Civil.ge reported.

sections.text: For Georgia, the opposition party led by former Prime Minister Giorgi Gakharia, has asked the Constitutional Court to examine its constitutionality in a separate case as the court starts hearing Georgian Dream's lawsuit to declare five opposition parties unconstitutional, executive secretary Berdia Sichinava said on 20 October, Civil.ge reported [3]. He called the bid to ban the only opposition party sitting in parliament 'absurd and devoid of any legal basis' and said it showed Georgian Dream sought to outlaw dissent [3]. The lawsuit, filed in October 2025 against three parties, was widened in April to the Federalists and in September to For Georgia [3]. No court ruling on the motion was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate, because one outlet reports the party's briefing; the motion itself was not read.

items.title: Georgia Accuses EU of Interference over Criticism of Opposition-Ban Case
items.lede: The ministry was answering Commission spokesperson Christian Wigand, who said the developments 'suggest a troubling instrumentalization of the justice system'.

sections.text: Georgia's Foreign Ministry said on 20 October that EU statements questioning the Constitutional Court proceedings on Georgian Dream's lawsuit to ban five opposition parties were 'an attempt to exert undue pressure' on the court and 'interference in Georgia's internal affairs', Civil.ge reported [4]. It urged EU representatives to refrain from statements that could prejudge the case and said recurring EU rhetoric hindered constructive engagement [4]. The statement followed European Commission spokesperson Christian Wigand's 19 October remark that the developments 'suggest a troubling instrumentalization of the justice system' [4]. OC Media reported the same statement and noted the European Parliament condemned the lawsuit in an 8 October resolution [5]. No further Commission reply was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high, because two outlets quote the ministry's statement and the Commission remark consistently.

items.title: Pashinyan Orders Reviews after Complaints of Coercion Before Local Elections
items.lede: Pashinyan sent the Inspection Body a claim of political dismissals and the Anti-Corruption Committee a child's campaign video, and pledged public accountability, Armenpress reported.

sections.text: Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan said he had received three messages after inviting voters and candidates to report illegal pressure ahead of local elections, Armenpress reported on 20 October [6]. He said he had ordered the Inspection Body to urgently review a Strong Armenia MP's claim that people were dismissed from jobs for political reasons, and had sent the Anti-Corruption Committee a video of a child giving a campaign speech [6]. Pashinyan had pledged to hold publicly to account any official found responsible [6]. No Inspection Body finding was published by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate, because the state news agency relays the prime minister's own post and no independent outlet was read; Armenpress does not corroborate its own government.

items.title: Georgia: UK-Sanctioned Imedi and POSTV Shares Change Hands for Nominal Sums
items.lede: Imedi's parent company is now held in four 25 percent parts by staff, including its director general, and Georgian Dream MP Viktor Japaridze sold his POSTV share, OC Media reported.

sections.text: Ownership of Georgian Media Production Group, which owns the pro-government channel Imedi, has been redistributed so that four people now hold 25 percent each, according to public registry documents reported by OC Media [7]. Prime Media Global sold its 50 percent share for ₾500 ($190), and two other shareholders gave up 10 percent each for ₾100 ($38) [7]. Director General Mariam Lomidze, host Irakli Chikhladze, and programming head Maia Chigoshvili each rose to 25 percent, and host Magda Anikashvili joined as a shareholder [7]. MP Viktor Japaridze, elected on the Georgian Dream list, sold his 52 percent share in POSTV for ₾1,000 ($380) [7]. Britain sanctioned both channels this year over what it called deliberate disinformation about Russia's invasion of Ukraine [7]. Chikhladze declined to comment [7].
Confidence is moderate, because one outlet reports the registry filings; the registry documents themselves were not read.

items.title: Former Russian Deputy Minister Named First Deputy Premier of Occupied Tskhinvali
items.lede: Ekaterina Tolstikova, who served in Dagestan's government from 2016 to 2020, replaces Dzambolat Tedeev under decrees by de facto leader Marat Kambolov, Interpressnews reported.

sections.text: Ekaterina Tolstikova, a former Russian deputy minister of education and science, was appointed 'first deputy prime minister' of Georgia's Russian-occupied Tskhinvali region by decree of its de facto leader Marat Kambolov, Interpressnews reported, citing the RES news agency [8]. A separate decree dismissed Dzambolat Tedeev from the post [8]. Tolstikova, born in Sevastopol in 1981, served as deputy chair of Dagestan's government from 2016 to 2020 and has advised the rector of the Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology since June 2026 [8]. No Georgian government comment was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate, because one Georgian outlet reports the decree on the word of the region's own news agency; the decree text was not read.

items.title: Azerbaijan Puts Seven in Türkiye on Wanted List over Hijab-Row Posts
items.lede: Azerbaijan put seven people in Türkiye on the international wanted list, and a Baku court ordered their detention in absentia over alleged calls to seize power.

sections.text: Azerbaijan's Prosecutor General's Office said seven people living or working in Türkiye, among them Haksöz writer Rıdvan Kaya, broadcaster Fatih Tezcan, and lawyer Ahmet Şanlı, are suspected of spreading calls between 25 September and 18 October to seize power by force, overturn the constitutional order, and incite religious hatred, APA reported [9]. The criminal case was opened on 16 October [9]. Armenpress later reported, citing the Prosecutor General's Office, that the seven were placed on the international wanted list and that Baku's Binagadi District Court ordered their detention in absentia [10]. OC Media reported that Amnesty International called on Baku to reverse restrictions on hijab-wearing pupils, that protests were held outside Azerbaijani missions in London, Berlin, and Ankara, and that Türkiye's embassy in Baku rejected Azerbaijani media claims about Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan's visit as unfounded [11]. No Turkish government response to the wanted-list step was found by the cutoff.

Confidence that the case, the wanted-list step, and the detention order exist is high, because APA and Armenpress carry the prosecutor's statement and OC Media reports the wider dispute. Confidence on the substance of the accusations is low, because no evidence has been published.

items.title: Doctors' Association Warns Insured Patients Face Longer Waits from 2027
items.lede: Doctors' association head Andreas Gassen said statutory patients will wait longer for appointments from next year because of outpatient cuts, a claim insurers called far-fetched.

sections.text: The head of the National Association of Statutory Health Insurance Physicians (KBV), Andreas Gassen, told Bild on Tuesday that patients with statutory insurance will wait longer for doctors' appointments from next year, saying federal cuts to outpatient funding had removed 'more than 50 million' appointments, the Stuttgarter Zeitung and tagesschau reported [1] [2]. Gassen criticised a rule in the recently passed emergency care reform that will require practices to report a fixed quota of free appointments to the appointment service, saying slots blocked this way are no longer available to the practices' own patients [1] [2]. According to the KBV, the government's savings programme for statutory health insurance cuts about €2.7 billion from outpatient care next year alone [2]. The head of the substitute insurers' association vdek, Ulrike Elsner, accused Gassen of deliberately stoking fear among millions of insured people and called the claim that millions of appointments would disappear far-fetched; she said mandatory reporting adds reliable referral by medical urgency without removing capacity [2]. No Health Ministry response was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is high that Gassen made these statements and that the vdek rejected them, because both outlets carry his quotes and tagesschau carries the vdek reply. The appointment figure is the KBV's own claim and is disputed.

items.title: AfD Confirms Hack as Unknown Group Posts About 421,000 Party Emails Online
items.lede: The AfD says only parts of a few mailboxes, most unused for years, were copied and that its federal association's current mailboxes were not affected.

sections.text: The AfD confirmed on Tuesday that a hosting provider used by the party was hacked in September 2026 and that parts of 'a few' mailboxes, most of them unused for years, were illegally copied, after unknown actors posted data online that they say comprises about 421,000 AfD emails, tagesschau and the Stuttgarter Zeitung reported [3] [4]. The AfD said current mailboxes of its federal association were not affected, that the attack was detected and stopped quickly, and that it is checking the publication [3] [4]. The leakers claim the data come from ten mailboxes, including one in the name of former party leader Alexander Gauland [3] [4]. Party sources told ARD the content appears authentic, and the AfD named its company Alternita as affected [3]. Bild reported that the files include a photo of the ID card of AfD deputy parliamentary leader Markus Frohnmaier, bank statements, and membership lists; this was not independently checked [3]. No statement from investigators was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is high that the AfD confirmed a September hack and that data were posted, because ARD and the Stuttgarter Zeitung quote the same party statement. Confidence is low on the size and authenticity of the leak and on its contents, which rest on the leakers' claims, Bild, and unnamed party sources.

items.title: Amazon Pledges More Than €16 Billion for Germany in 2027 at Berlin Summit
items.lede: It is unclear whether the sum includes earlier AWS pledges of €8.8 billion for Frankfurt and €7.8 billion for Brandenburg, the Stuttgarter Zeitung noted.

sections.text: Amazon announced on Tuesday at the federal government's Invest in Germany Summit in Berlin that it plans to invest more than €16 billion in Germany in 2027, including €4.8 billion to expand its AWS Europe (Frankfurt) cloud and AI region [5] [6]. The company said the money also covers its Leo satellite network, robotic logistics, and more than 15 Prime Video productions [5]. Economy Minister Katherina Reiche called the investment 'a clear vote of confidence' in Germany as a business location [5] [6]. The Stuttgarter Zeitung noted that Amazon gave few further details and that it is unclear whether the sum includes earlier AWS pledges of €8.8 billion for Frankfurt and €7.8 billion for Brandenburg [6]. Chancellor Friedrich Merz told the summit that several companies had pledged a total of €800 billion by 2028, while Reiche told Deutschlandfunk the pledges amount to €228 billion counting only projects over €100 million; the timeframe and basis of the figures were not given [7].

Confidence is high that the pledge was announced and on its headline figures, because they come from Amazon's own release and the Stuttgarter Zeitung reports them. How much of the sum is new money is not established, and the government's summit totals conflict and come without a breakdown.

items.title: Baden-Württemberg Launches Task Force to Halve Power Grid Expansion Times
items.lede: Özdemir said grids in some regions, above all Mittelbaden, are reaching their limits, and the results will feed a state grid acceleration law.

sections.text: Baden-Württemberg's state government launched a task force on Tuesday at a kick-off event in Stuttgart's Liederhalle to speed up expansion of the electricity distribution grid, the state government and dpa reported [8] [9]. Minister-President Cem Özdemir (Greens) said procedures that now take up to ten years should be cut to five, and said existing grids in some regions, above all Mittelbaden, are reaching their limits [9] [8]. Energy Minister Thekla Walker (Greens) said the work will focus on digitalisation, prioritising projects and regions, better use of existing infrastructure, and faster approval of new substations, with the results to go into a state grid acceleration law [9] [8]. Ministries, authorities, grid operators, businesses, storage operators, and municipalities take part; the task force, agreed in the Greens-CDU coalition agreement, is to run for two years with a review after one [9]. Torsten Höck of the energy and water association VfEW said capacity is so scarce in some regions that connection requests cannot always be met, and that the expansion needs 'many billions' [9] [8].
Confidence is high, because the state government's release and dpa report the same launch, aims, and participants. The investment figure is the association's estimate.

items.title: Berlin SPD and Greens Vote to Open Coalition Talks with the Left
items.lede: If the Left's 31 October congress agrees, talks could start in early November, and Elif Eralp could become the party's first Governing Mayor of Berlin.

sections.text: The Berlin SPD state board voted 26 to 3 at a digital meeting on Monday evening to open coalition talks with the Left and the Greens, and a small Greens party congress then backed talks with only 2 of 45 delegates against, tagesschau and dpa reported [10] [11]. The Left, which won the 20 September election with 25.7 percent, decides at a party congress on 31 October, and talks could start in early November [10] [11]. If they succeed, Left parliamentary leader Elif Eralp could become the party's first Governing Mayor of Berlin [10]. SPD state leaders Bettina König and Steffen Krach said the joint statements on antisemitism and organised crime remain the basic condition for working together, and Greens state leader Nina Stahr said the Left 'has in parts a problem with antisemitism' [11]. The exploratory paper agreed on Saturday includes socialising about 160,000 flats owned by large housing companies, with up to €16 billion set aside for compensation, and a new-build programme for 100,000 flats [12] [10] [11]. Before the votes, SPD parliamentary leader Matthias Miersch voiced 'considerable doubts', and 20 SPD MPs opposed the talks [13].
Confidence is high, because tagesschau and dpa report the same vote counts and timetable, citing party figures. The Left's decision is still to come.

items.title: Federal Government Signs AI Letter of Intent with Nvidia at Investment Summit
items.lede: The Economy and Research ministries signed a letter of intent with Nvidia on 19 October to develop advanced AI models for robots and other physical AI systems.

sections.text: The Economy and Research ministries signed a letter of intent with US chipmaker Nvidia on Monday to push an initiative to develop advanced AI models for 'physical AI', meaning AI built into systems such as robots, the federal government said at the first Invest in Germany summit in Berlin, tagesschau reported [14]. The government said the aim is to bring industrial AI into broad use, and that Nvidia will open its AI models to smaller firms and research institutes [14]. Chancellor Friedrich Merz urged companies to open their industrial data for AI, and Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang said the company invested almost $1 billion in Germany last year [14] [15]. The government gave no figure for its own spending; tagesschau cited a media report that it plans to back the project with a three-digit million-euro sum, partly to rent computing capacity in Deutsche Telekom's AI cloud [14]. The letter of intent itself was not found on a government site by the cutoff.

Confidence is high that the letter of intent was signed and on its stated aims, because tagesschau quotes the federal statement and dpa reports the same event. The funding figure rests on an unnamed media report cited by tagesschau and is not confirmed by the government.

New research covered 05:10 CEST to 17:10 CEST on 20 October; items from the previous edition whose times fall inside the 24 hours were carried and re-checked, stories with new developments are marked as follow-ups, and items older than 24 hours were dropped. The priority story remains France: targeted curfews were renewed after a calm first night, Justice Minister Darmanin said 149 rioters or looters had been jailed as the custody count passed 2,500, and Interior Minister Nuñez told prefects to ban risky Saturday protests as scrutiny of police baton use and grenade injuries continued. Italy is sending 500 troops to Milan, and Storm Adam's toll in Spain rose to seven. Russian drones killed seven people around Kyiv and caused outages in 12 regions, shelling killed three heat-plant workers in Kramatorsk, and Zelensky met US envoy Witkoff in Oslo. The NATO Council set Black Sea talks after Romania downed two drones, Lithuania sought a NATO rule change on shooting down drones, Albania's protests reached an eighth day with 271 arrests, Georgia accused the EU of interference over the opposition-ban case, and the AfD confirmed a hack as about 421,000 party emails were posted online.
